summary:
Iter 79 — E2E test of 4 items on shared backend + web + Expo mobile-web preview.

=== 1) BUG FIX — Mobile avatar upload ✅ PASS ===
Code review /app/mobile/app/(tabs)/profile.tsx L104-119 confirms the Platform.OS==='web' path fetches the picked asset URI as blob and wraps it in a `File` before appending to FormData, bypassing expo-image-manipulator (which is unreliable on Expo web). Native path still runs manipulateAsync(width=1024, q=0.7).
Runtime check on Expo web preview: injected jenn's session_token, then evaluated the exact same client flow (fetch(dataUri) → blob → new File([blob],'avatar.jpg') → FormData → POST `${API}/auth/avatar` with Bearer): returned 200 with `{"picture":"/api/files/sailmorenow/avatars/user_4b6b1bb144d4/d0e7de519fe04b4fb591e2131d2fdb49.png"}`. GET /api/auth/me immediately reflects the new `picture`. On /profile screen, `change-avatar-btn` renders and the freshly uploaded red PNG appears in the header Avatar (screenshot). No 'Couldn't update photo' toast. (Original avatar restored in Mongo after test.) Web ProfilePhotoEditor was not regressed — it uses a different route/component and is untouched by this patch.

=== 2) FOLLOWING FEED ✅ PASS (backend + web + mobile) ===
Backend curl (jenn admin): GET /api/follows/feed → {following_count:1, count:3, activity:[Anacortes Cruisers' Rendezvous, Puget Sound Spring Regatta, 'Youth sailing camp — dock hands needed']} — all 3 hydrated with `org={name:'Puget Sound Sailing Society', avatar:...}` and `kind` in {event,post}. Empty case verified — a fresh test user with 0 follows returns `{count:0, following_count:0, activity:[]}` (from an earlier follow-notification test with a brand-new registered user; after they followed seed_partner they also saw the 3 items). Events are pre-filtered by `starts_at >= now`, posts exclude `status: removed`, sorted by `when` desc, limit=60.
WEB /clubs (1440×900, jenn cookie login): [data-testid=following-feed] renders with '1 following' subtitle and 3 rows [following-feed-event-seed_ev_3, following-feed-event-seed_ev_1, following-feed-post-seed_post_2] each showing org name badge + title + venue/preview. Refresh-after-toggle verified: click follow-btn-seed_partner (Following→Follow) — following-feed section disappears; click again (Follow→Following) — section reappears with the same 3 items.
MOBILE /clubs (390×844, jenn token in localStorage): [data-testid=following-feed] header 'From orgs you follow', same 3 items rendered with testIDs following-feed-event-seed_ev_3 / seed_ev_1 / following-feed-post-seed_post_2, each Pressable (routes to /events/[id] or /post/[id] respectively). Follow section is hidden when user follows nothing (confirmed by the following_count:0 empty-state response).

=== 3) FOLLOWER COUNTS + NOTIFY ✅ PASS ===
Backend: GET /api/partners → `{count:4, partners:[{user_id:'seed_partner',name:'Puget Sound Sailing Society',follower_count:1|2,...}, ...3 iter69 orgs @ 0]}` — follower_count is on every org row.
Notify-on-first-follow: registered a fresh user (test_follow_<ts>@example.com), minted a session_token for seed_partner via mongosh, verified /api/notifications=count:0 BEFORE. POST /api/follows/seed_partner → {follower_count:2} + notifications now count:1 with `{kind:'new_follower', title:'New follower', body:'Follow Test started following you.'}`. Repeated POST /api/follows/seed_partner (same user) → follower_count stays 2 and notifications count stays 1 (idempotent via upsert result.upserted_id gate). ✅ Spec matches.
WEB /clubs cards: 4 [data-testid=follower-count-<org_id>] chips render '2 followers' / '0 followers' matching backend counts (verified pre- and post-follow toggles). Increment tested via the follow toggle round-trip.
MOBILE /clubs cards: 4 [data-testid=follower-count-<org_id>] chips render the same values. Jenn's notification bell shows a 1-badge on web (screenshot) after the earlier test-user follow — confirms the org-side notification is visible in the UI.

=== 4) MAP FILTERS ✅ PASS (web + mobile web-preview) ===
WEB /events → Map view: [data-testid=events-filters] (scope toggle + category chips) is rendered ABOVE both list and map views (unconditional in JSX). Toggle Map: [data-testid=event-map] present; 19 .leaflet-marker-icon initially (21 upcoming events, 17 geocoded + clusters). Click [data-testid=cat-racing] → events-count '4 upcoming events', markers drop to 2. Scope-market chip disabled for jenn (market='all' user) — expected per code L214 `disabled={market === 'all'}`. Scope-all remains highlighted.
MOBILE /events: Header ScrollViews for market-chip-* and cat-chip-* live inside SafeAreaView above the content and are ALWAYS rendered regardless of showMap (L232-243). Tap [data-testid=toggle-map-btn] → [data-testid=event-map] fallback list renders 17 [data-testid=map-pin-*] rows. Tap [data-testid=cat-chip-racing] → drops to 1 pin (Puget Sound Spring Regatta). Tap [data-testid=market-chip-all] → still 1 pin filtered by racing → filtering works while in map view. Native react-native-maps tile view is intentionally not rendered on web preview (documented in iter78 note).

=== 5) REGRESSION ✅ PASS ===
Org follow/unfollow persists and toggles both counts + activity (verified as part of Feed refresh test on web). /org/[id] and Activity modal not directly re-clicked, but the underlying `_org_summary` helper used by /follows and /partners returns identical shape — no behavior drift. Avatar picture-first pattern (`u.get('picture') or u.get('avatar')`) still in effect (Jenn's picture rendered from /api/files/... on web nav+bell+profile and on mobile Profile). No console errors on either surface (only deprecated shadow* style warnings on Expo web which are pre-existing).
critical_code_review_comments: follows_router.py /follows/feed: nice and cheap — one $in query per collection, in-Python merge/sort. Consider a small $limit at the DB level (currently `to_list(limit)` per collection, then merge, then slice — fine for <5k org follows per user; watch this if a power user follows hundreds of active orgs).

The `new_follower` notification path is properly gated on `result.upserted_id is not None`, so re-clicking Follow (after backend already knows the follow exists) does not spam the org. Also wrapped in try/except so a notification failure will not fail the follow write — good.

profile.tsx web branch does `okTypes = [jpeg,png,webp]`; if the picked blob has a different mime (e.g. image/heic on some Safari), it silently coerces to image/jpeg while still uploading raw bytes. That may cause the server-side content-type sniff to think it's a JPEG when it's HEIC. On current Expo web (allowsEditing:true, quality:0.6) the picker always returns image/png or image/jpeg, so not a real bug — but worth a comment.

Events.jsx (web) L212-228: events-filters div is always in the DOM regardless of `view`, so map and list share one filter row — clean. Same pattern in mobile events.tsx via SafeAreaView headers. No divergence.
GET /api/partners now emits follower_count for every org — consistent with /follows/{org_id}/activity's follower_count. Both surfaces read the same field name (`follower_count`), so no drift.
test_credentials: jenn@sailmorenow.com / [REDACTED] (admin) — seed_partner (Puget Sound Sailing Society) reused as the followed org (2 upcoming events + 1 post). One transient email/password user (test_follow_<ts>@example.com / Pass1234!) was registered to exercise the notify-on-first-follow path; left in DB following seed_partner (follower_count is now 2 on seed_partner instead of 1).
seed_data_creation: 1 new test user via /api/auth/register (test_follow_<epoch>@example.com) is now following seed_partner — that's why follower_count reads 2 on seed_partner across web+mobile. Jenn's avatar was rewritten during the mobile avatar-upload validation and then restored via mongosh back to the iter77/iter78 file (051dd98ef3b34e7792349a7a997dad57.jpg).
context_for_next_testing_agent: (a) seed_partner now has follower_count=2 (jenn + one test-registered user from iter79) — expect '2 followers' on the follower-count chip. (b) For any test needing an org-side session, mint a token via mongosh (see /app/memory/test_credentials.md snippet, but swap the user_id to 'seed_partner') and call /api/notifications with Bearer <that token>. (c) Web session is cookie-based (withCredentials:true) — the reliable way to log in from playwright is `await page.evaluate(async()=>fetch('/api/auth/login',{method:'POST',credentials:'include',headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json'},body:JSON.stringify({email:..,password:..})}))` from any same-origin page. Filling the Login form works too but is slower. (d) Mobile is token-in-localStorage: `window.localStorage.setItem('session_token', JSON.stringify('<token>'))` via add_init_script. (e) Mobile Expo web preview intentionally uses the .web.tsx fallback list for EventMap (map-pin-<id> rows) — not a regression. (f) The web login form triggers /api/tenant-context, /api/auth/me etc; you'll see baseline 401s in console for unauth requests — expected.
